message.content:
You are adding translations (i18n) to the "bring your own Deepgram key" screens of a Next.js 16 app ("Heard": live captions for YouTube livestreams). Repo: /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions, web app in apps/web. Other agents are editing OTHER files at the same time; only edit the files listed as yours. Do not commit, stash, reset or switch branches.

The i18n setup is already built (read first, do not change):
- apps/web/src/i18n/config.ts (locales en, es, fr, pt, de, ja)
- apps/web/src/i18n/I18nProvider.tsx: client hook `useT("key")` returns the current language's object for the "key" area.
- apps/web/src/i18n/messages/en/common.ts and es/common.ts show the pattern: the English file exports a plain object; each other language does `import type { key as en } from "../en/key"; export const key: typeof en = {...}` so TypeScript forces the same shape. Functions allowed for interpolation (e.g. a masked key or counts).

Your files:
- apps/web/src/components/DeepgramKeyDialog.tsx, DeepgramKeyForm.tsx, DeepgramKeySettings.tsx, ByokNote.tsx (grep apps/web/src for any other key-related component with UI text, e.g. in src/lib/deepgram-key.ts user-facing messages; if a user-facing message string lives in a lib file, return a code from the lib and translate in the component, or leave the lib alone if it is not shown to users)
- apps/web/src/i18n/messages/{en,es,fr,pt,de,ja}/key.ts (currently `{}`; fill them)

Important: these screens explain who pays and where the key goes (it stays in the browser and is only sent to Deepgram). Translate that meaning precisely; do not soften or change what is promised. Keep the English exactly as it is today. Do not change any logic about where the key is stored or sent (see AGENTS.md rules in the repo root: a user's own key stays in their browser and only goes to Deepgram).

Never translate "Heard", "Deepgram", "YouTube", "Chrome", URLs. Natural concise UI copy (Spanish neutral Latin American, Portuguese Brazilian, Japanese polite and short).

When done run: cd apps/web && PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.1/bin:$PATH npx tsc --noEmit -p .  (the default node on PATH is broken; always use that prefix). Other agents may cause unrelated errors in their own files; only fix yours. Do NOT start/stop the dev server.

Report back: files changed, anything left in English and why, tsc result.

content.text:
I've translated all four bring-your-own-key screens into es, fr, pt, de and ja, and the English reads exactly as it did before. `tsc --noEmit` passes with no errors. I haven't looked at any of the screens in a browser.

**Files changed** (all under `apps/web/src`):
- `i18n/messages/en/key.ts` holds the English strings, moved over word for word. They're grouped by screen: `dialog`, `form` (including `errors`), `settings` and `byok`.
- `i18n/messages/{es,fr,pt,de,ja}/key.ts` are the five translations, each typed against the English file so they must have the same shape.
- `components/DeepgramKeyDialog.tsx`, `DeepgramKeyForm.tsx`, `DeepgramKeySettings.tsx` and `ByokNote.tsx` now read their text with `useT("key")`.

**How the form errors work now:** the form used to store the English error sentence. It now stores a code (`empty`, `malformed`, `rejected` or `offline`) and looks up the translated message when it displays it. The `rejected` and `offline` codes come straight from `verifyDeepgramKey`.

**Logic:** nothing changed in how the key is stored or where it's sent. `lib/deepgram-key.ts` has no text that users see, so I left it alone.

**Promises kept in every language:** "stays in this browser", "goes only to Deepgram", "Heard's server never sees it", and that new accounts get free credit. In Japanese I wrote the key "stays inside this browser" (ブラウザ内に留まり) rather than "is saved in this browser", because "stays" is the actual promise.

**Left in English on purpose:**
- Heard, Deepgram and the `console.deepgram.com` link, as you asked.
- The role name "Member", because that is the label Deepgram's console shows.
- The masked key (`••••1a2b`), which isn't text.
